correctness.rationale: The clipped product identity and the Gram determinants give exact Euclidean volume and surface area. The quotient classification follows by reducing to z versus T, proving z>1 for p>=4 and p=3,q>=5, and proving z>T for p=2,q>=7 by a strict quadratic Taylor bound. The last seven cases have rational interval certificates from the delivered script. Eleven independent orthogonal-projection convex-hull checks corroborate the metric formulas. Finite checks are not substituted for the unbounded analytic steps.

value.rationale: Deleting a single graph edge is a canonical geometric perturbation; the Euclidean isoperimetric quotient is a natural scale-invariant efficiency measure. All deleted polytopes have smaller area and volume, yet the quotient reverses sign at exactly four small part-size pairs; the theorem fully classifies the reversal and separates exponential balanced response from polynomial fixed-part response.
